definition_zh: 公然的；明目张胆的；刺眼的；喧哗刺耳的
definition_en: done openly and unashamedly, or offensively conspicuous
core_image: 考试时把课本摊在桌上抄的人
scene: 监考老师转身的一瞬，他把答案摊得明明白白。It was a blatant attempt to buy votes.
sceneCN: 这里 blatant 是「公然的、明目张胆的」（第 1 个义项：毫不掩饰地做出可耻之事）；句意是这是一次明目张胆的买票企图。

pos.zh: 公然的；明目张胆的；刺眼的

derivatives.zh: blatant 加 -ly，义为「公然地；赤裸裸地」

senses.title: Openly shameless in wrongdoing
senses.definition: doing something bad openly, without trying to hide it
senses.example: It was a blatant attempt to buy votes.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一次明目张胆的买票企图。
senses.why: The old sense of loud coarse noise shifted to loud, coarse behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 旧义「喧闹粗哑之声」转移到「喧闹粗鄙之行」。

senses.title: Offensively conspicuous
senses.definition: so obvious and loud that it offends the eye or mind
senses.definitionCN: 过于显眼张扬以致令人反感
senses.example: The blatant logo covered the whole jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 那枚巨大的商标铺满了整件外套。
senses.why: What shouts at the senses earns the name of the shouting word.
senses.whyCN: 向感官叫嚷之物便承袭了「叫嚷」之词。

senses.title: Of lies, utterly obvious
senses.definition: of a lie or falsehood, so bare that no one can miss it
senses.definitionCN: 谎言赤裸到无人可以忽视
senses.example: His excuse was a blatant lie from start to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 他的借口从头到尾都是明摆着的谎话。
senses.why: A lie too loud to hide is described with the loudness word.
senses.whyCN: 响亮到藏不住的谎言，便以「响亮」之词形容。

senses.title: Showing total disregard
senses.definition: expressing complete indifference to rules or feelings
senses.definitionCN: 对规则或他人感受表现出全然的漠视
senses.example: The factory showed blatant disregard for safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂对安全规章全然不顾。
senses.why: Ignoring rules loudly is a form of noisiness toward society.
senses.whyCN: 大张旗鼓地无视规则，是对社会的一种「喧哗」。

senses.title: Of advertising, crudely direct
senses.definition: of promotion, crudely direct and without subtlety
senses.definitionCN: 推销方式生硬直接、毫无含蓄
senses.example: The film was spoiled by blatant product placement.
senses.exampleCN: 赤裸裸的植入广告毁了这部电影。
senses.why: Sales talk that shouts has the same coarse loudness as the old sense.
senses.whyCN: 叫卖式的推销与旧义的粗响一脉相承。

senses.title: Of manner, aggressively forward
senses.definition: of behaviour, pushy and aggressive in a way that jars
senses.definitionCN: 举止咄咄逼人、令人不适
senses.example: Her blatant self-promotion annoyed the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她张扬的自我推销惹恼了整个团队。
senses.why: Pushiness is noise made with the body instead of the voice.
senses.whyCN: 张扬是身体代替喉咙发出的噪音。

senses.title: Of colour or design, glaring
senses.definition: of colour or style, glaring and lacking taste
senses.definitionCN: 色彩或风格俗艳刺目、缺乏品位
senses.example: Blatant wallpaper made the room unbearable.
senses.exampleCN: 艳俗的墙纸让房间令人难以忍受。
senses.why: Loud colours literally make visual noise.
senses.whyCN: 扎眼的色彩正是视觉上的「噪音」。

senses.title: Of sounds, coarse and noisy (older use)
senses.definition: of sound, loud, harsh, and coarse, the original sense
senses.definitionCN: 声音响亮粗厉，为该词本义
senses.example: The blatant horns announced the procession.
senses.exampleCN: 粗亮的号角宣告了队伍的到来。
senses.why: Coined for loud flapping or quacking noise before any moral sense existed.
senses.whyCN: 该词最初即为形容粗厉声响而造，后才生出道德义。

intro.en: Blatant was coined by Edmund Spenser for loud, coarse noise.
intro.cn: blatant 由斯宾塞所创，本指粗厉喧闹之声。

items.en: Edmund Spenser coined blatant in The Faerie Queene for a blatant beast with a thousand tongues, a figure of slander.
items.cn: 1596 年斯宾塞在《仙后》中创造 blatant，形容「千舌诽谤兽」的喧噪。

items.en: probably imitative, echoing Latin blatire, to gossip or babble.
items.cn: 一般认为系拟声造词，或受拉丁语 blatire「喋喋闲聊」影响。

items.en: in 17th-century Scots it meant filthy or loose in morals.
items.cn: 17 世纪苏格兰用法中指品行污秽放荡。

items.en: the sound sense faded as the sense of offensively obvious wrongdoing grew.
items.cn: 17 至 19 世纪间，声音义渐衰，「扎眼的公然冒犯」义渐盛。

items.en: now standard for anything shamelessly obvious.
items.cn: 今为标准词，泛指一切无耻的明目张胆。

note.en: Blatant has no common relatives; look-alikes sound similar, and near-meanings gather shameless-obvious words.
note.cn: blatant 无常见同族词；形近组收音近词，近义组收无耻外露类词。

entries.definitionCN: 喋喋废话——音近词源不同
聒噪闲扯——声音联想相近
烈火——拼写相近，词义无关
公然恶劣的——最易混淆的近义词
厚颜无耻的——偏胆大不羞

normalIntro.en: Blatant began as Spenser's loud beast, now it means shamelessly obvious.
normalIntro.cn: blatant 始于斯宾塞笔下喧噪之兽，今指无耻的明目张胆。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with flagrant, though they overlap.
normal.cn: 勿与 flagrant 混淆，尽管二者有重叠。

normal.en: A blatant lie is one everyone can see.
normal.cn: blatant lie 指人人看得出的大谎。

normal.en: Its first use described a monster of slander.

abstract.en: See a student copying from a book left wide open.
abstract.cn: 看一个学生对着摊开的书本公然抄袭。

abstract.en: Hear a car radio so loud the street vibrates.
abstract.cn: 听车载音响响到整条街都在震动。

abstract.en: Picture a sign painted across an entire mountain.
abstract.cn: 想象涂满整座山的巨幅招牌。

examples.en: It was a blatant attempt to buy votes.
examples.cn: 这是一次明目张胆的买票企图。

examples.en: The factory showed blatant disregard for safety rules.
examples.cn: 这家工厂对安全规章全然不顾。

examples.en: The film was spoiled by blatant product placement.
examples.cn: 赤裸裸的植入广告毁了这部电影。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不来等他」——小偷不来等他，明抢了：行事 blatantly（明目张胆）到毫不遮掩。

root: 1596 年 Edmund Spenser 在《仙后》中创造的词，形容「千舌诽谤兽」的粗厉喧噪；一般认为系拟声造词，或受拉丁语 blatire「喋喋闲语」影响；后由「喧闹刺耳」转为「明目张胆、刺眼张扬」。

sensesIntro.en: From a slanderous beast's noise to shameless openness, blatant always means too loud to miss.
sensesIntro.cn: 从诽谤兽的喧噪到无耻的张扬，blatant 总指「响亮到无法忽视」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a textbook left wide open on the exam desk
core.cn: 核心意象：考桌上摊开的教科书

branches.en: Things that shout at the eye

intro.en: Blatant is a literary coinage with few derivatives.
intro.cn: blatant 是文学造词，派生词不多。

latinIntro.cn: 或与拉丁语 blatire 有回响。

items.meaningCN: 喋喋闲语（可能的词源回响）
